- Model tends to underestimate prices in early forecast windows (especially 30d) when sentiment is neutral or negative, leading to persistent lag.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history, particularly when model reacts too aggressively to recent highs.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after sustained upward moves, then undercorrects downward in subsequent periods.
- Sentiment > 0.00 correlates with higher forecast accuracy; when sentiment is flat or negative, model underperforms, especially in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30d window; model should adjust downward early if sentiment is weak or stable.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent history” — forecasts often mirror recent price patterns too closely, ignoring longer-term trends or sentiment shifts.
